provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: BECE arts theory marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list elements of art, explain music theory concepts, and solve past questions.
Introduction:
We have learned about basic art elements and music theory. This week we will practice BECE questions to prepare for the exam.
Content:
Elements of art include line, shape, colour, texture and form. Music theory covers notes, scales, rhythm and harmony. Practice questions from past BECE papers will be solved in class. Examples include identifying Nigerian traditional art forms and explaining how they reflect our culture.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to solve 10 past BECE theory questions and present their answers to the class.
Evaluation questions:
1. List three elements of art.
2. What is the difference between major and minor scales?
3. Explain how Benin bronze art reflects Nigerian culture.
4. Solve this question: What is the primary colour?
Summary:
This week we reviewed art theory and music concepts through past questions to improve our exam skills.

topics.title: BECE arts history marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify Nigerian artists, explain traditional art forms, and discuss cultural significance.
Introduction:
We have studied Nigerian art traditions and famous artists. This week we will focus on history questions for the BECE exam.
Content:
Nigerian artists include Ben Enwonwu, Bruce Onobrakpeya and Nmadinachi Egwu. Traditional art forms include Nok terracotta, Ife bronze and Igbo Ukwu. Each reflects our cultural heritage. Harmattan season influences traditional art materials like clay and wood used by our ancestors.
Class activity:
Students will create a timeline of Nigerian art history and match famous artworks to their cultural periods.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name two Nigerian contemporary artists.
2. Explain the cultural significance of Nok terracotta.
3. How does the harmattan season influence traditional art making?
4. Differentiate between Ife and Benin bronze art styles.
Summary:
We practiced art history questions focusing on Nigerian artists and traditions to strengthen our exam knowledge.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full exam paper under timed conditions, identify their weak areas, and suggest improvements.
Introduction:
We have practiced individual topics. This week we will take a full mock BECE exam to test our overall knowledge.
Content:
The mock exam will cover all topics from the term including art theory, history, music and practical skills. Students must work under exam conditions with time limits. After completing, we will mark papers together and discuss common mistakes. Like a market trader checking goods, we must examine our work carefully.
Class activity:
Students will complete a full BECE mock paper in timed conditions, then swap papers for peer marking before class discussion.
Evaluation questions:
1. How did you manage your time during the mock exam?
2. Which topic was most challenging and why?
3. What strategies will you use to improve your weak areas?
4. Explain one mistake you made and how to avoid it next time.
Summary:
The mock exam helped us identify strengths and weaknesses before the real BECE examination.

topics.title: Project: graduation arts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create a graduation art piece, explain their artistic choices, and present their work.
Introduction:
We have learned various art techniques throughout the year. This week we will focus on creating graduation-themed artwork for our final project.
Content:
Graduation art projects can include paintings, sculptures or mixed media pieces reflecting our journey in JSS. Students should choose materials like canvas, clay or recycled materials. The artwork should symbolize growth, achievement and transition to the next level of education.
Class activity:
Students will create their graduation art piece using materials provided, then write a short explanation of their artistic choices and symbolism.
Evaluation questions:
1. What materials did you use for your graduation art piece?
2. Explain the symbolism in your artwork.
3. How does your piece reflect your school experience?
4. What challenges did you face while creating your project?
Summary:
We created meaningful graduation artwork that represents our academic journey and artistic development.

topics.title: Performance project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to prepare a performance piece, demonstrate proper execution, and critique peer performances.
Introduction:
We have studied various performing arts including music, dance and drama. This week we will focus on preparing performance pieces for our final project.
Content:
Performance projects can include traditional dances like the Ekombi, musical performances on instruments like the talking drum, or dramatic scenes. Students should practice timing, expression and coordination. Like actors in a Nollywood film, we must convey emotion and tell a story through our performance.
Class activity:
Students will perform their prepared pieces for the class and receive constructive feedback from peers and teacher.
Evaluation questions:
1. What type of performance did you prepare and why?
2. Explain how you incorporated cultural elements into your performance.
3. What feedback did you receive and how will you improve?
4. How did practicing help your final performance?
Summary:
We developed and performed artistic pieces that showcase our creative abilities and cultural understanding.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their weak areas in arts, create improvement plans, and practice targeted exercises.
Introduction:
We have completed mock exams and projects. This week we will focus on strengthening our weak areas through targeted practice.
Content:
Students should identify topics where they performed poorly in previous assessments. Common weaknesses include art history dates, music theory concepts, or practical techniques. We will create individual improvement plans and practice specific exercises to build confidence in these areas.
Class activity:
Students will work in small groups based on shared weak areas, creating and solving practice questions together.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is your weakest area in cultural and creative arts?
2. What specific exercises will help you improve?
3. How has your understanding of weak topics improved this week?
4. Explain how you can continue practicing at home.
Summary:
We identified and improved our weak areas through focused practice and targeted exercises.

topics.title: Portfolio completion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to select their best works, organize them effectively, and present a professional portfolio.
Introduction:
We have created various artworks throughout the term. This week we will complete our portfolios by selecting and organizing our best pieces.
Content:
A portfolio showcases an artist's best work and growth over time. Students should select 5-7 pieces that demonstrate their skills and creativity. Works should be properly mounted, labeled with title, date and medium. Like a market display, the portfolio should present your work attractively and professionally.
Class activity:
Students will mount their selected artworks on portfolio paper, write artist statements, and arrange their portfolios for final review.
Evaluation questions:
1. What criteria did you use to select your portfolio pieces?
2. How does your portfolio show your artistic growth?
3. What challenges did you face while organizing your portfolio?
4. Explain how you can improve your portfolio presentation.
Summary:
We completed our portfolios by selecting and presenting our best artistic works in a professional manner.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete tasks under time pressure, improve their accuracy, and develop exam strategies.
Introduction:
We have practiced individual skills and concepts. This week we will focus on improving our speed and accuracy for the BECE exam.
Content:
Speed and accuracy are crucial for exam success. Students will practice timed exercises including quick sketches, music notation, and theory questions. We will develop strategies like scanning questions before answering and managing time effectively. Like a danfo driver navigating traffic, we must be quick but careful.
Class activity:
Students will complete timed mini-tests in different art disciplines, then discuss strategies for improving speed without sacrificing accuracy.
Evaluation questions:
1. What strategies help you complete tasks quickly and accurately?
2. How did your performance improve with practice?
3. What time management techniques work best for you?
4. Explain how to balance speed and accuracy during exams.
Summary:
We developed skills to work efficiently and accurately under time pressure for the upcoming BECE examination.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to simulate exam conditions, apply all learned knowledge, and evaluate their performance.
Introduction:
We have practiced throughout the term. This week we will take our final mock exam to prepare for the real BECE examination.
Content:
The final mock exam will replicate the actual BECE format including timing, question types and marking scheme. Students must demonstrate knowledge of art theory, history, music and practical skills. After completion, we will conduct a thorough review of answers and discuss exam techniques. Like preparing for a traditional wedding ceremony, we must be fully prepared.
Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock exam under strict exam conditions, then participate in a detailed review session discussing answers and exam strategies.
Evaluation questions:
1. How did this mock exam compare to previous ones?
2. What areas showed the most improvement?
3. What final preparations will you make before the real exam?
4. Explain how you will manage exam day stress.
Summary:
Our final mock exam provided comprehensive practice and identified any remaining areas needing improvement before BECE.

topics.title: BECE readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain exam day procedures, demonstrate confidence in their knowledge, and prepare mentally for the exam.
Introduction:
We have completed all preparation activities. This week we will finalize our readiness for the BECE examination.
Content:
Exam day tips include arriving early, bringing required materials like pencils and erasers, reading instructions carefully, and managing time wisely. Students should get adequate rest the night before and eat a good breakfast. Like a farmer before harvest, we must be fully prepared and confident. We will also have a motivational send-off session.
Class activity:
Students will create personal exam day checklists and participate in a group discussion about managing exam stress and staying confident.
Evaluation questions:
1. What materials must you bring to the BECE exam?
2. How will you manage your time during the exam?
3. What strategies will help you stay calm during the test?
4. Explain how you have prepared for the arts portion of BECE.
Summary:
We finalized our exam preparation and built confidence for success in the upcoming BECE examination.
